Patients with cancer are at increased risk of thromboem- bolic disease, and thrombosis can be the earliest clinical sign of malignancy.1 The risk of thromboembolism may be further increased by the use of antineoplastics. Deep-vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism have been reported with a variety of chemotherapeutic regimens.
